title: A measured record has three layers: a scale in millimetres, a signal in time, and a regime label on top
summary: The time series gives height and width against time with colour bands naming the stage of the flame. The kymograph unrolls the whole flame into one time-height image, so that moving structures appear as slanted stripes. The tracking clip shows where the scale comes from: a ruler beside the burner tube.

media.alt: Time series of flame height (black) and flame width (dark red) in millimetres against time from about minus 10 to 535 seconds for run MVI_8036, n-heptane. Height climbs from about 5 mm to about 55 mm by 155 s, then becomes a dense jagged trace between about 60 and 150 mm. Width rises to about 20 mm near 100 s, then stays at about 11 to 14 mm. Coloured bands behind: red Ignition Transient to about 155 s, green Steady Laminar to about 180 s, then alternating tan Flickering Onset and blue Periodic Flickering.

source.caption: Height and width with regime bands
source.note: Three measurement views of the same pool-flame run family: a full-record height and width time series with regime colour bands (run MVI_8036), a kymograph (flame width against height and time) for the onset window, and an earlier burner-tracking clip in which a ruler gives the pixel scale. The page teaches how a measured record is put on a physical scale and then split into regimes.

read_the_figure.question: How do the flame's height and width evolve through the run, and when does the flame switch from steady burning to flickering?
read_the_figure.axes: Time series: x is time in seconds after ignition (about -10 to 535 s), y is height and width in mm on one shared axis (about 0 to 160). Kymograph: x is time (s), y is height above the burner (mm, 0 to about 170), colour is the local flame width in pixels (about 0 to 240). Tracking clip: a frame of the burner tube beside a ruler, with a white box marking the region tracked.
look_at: Black line (height): a smooth rise during the ignition transient, then a jagged cloud once flicker sets in. The jaggedness, not the mean, is the flicker.
Dark red line (width): it starts later than the height trace (about 35 s) and is almost flat at about 11 to 14 mm. Width changes are small compared with height changes.

Background bands: red is Ignition Transient (to about 155 s), green Steady Laminar (about 155 to 181 s), tan Flickering Onset and blue Periodic Flickering after that. After about 180 s the tan and blue bands alternate many times.

Kymograph: bright yellow-white means a wide flame at that height and time; the dark top edge is the flame tip, so the upper boundary of the colour is the height trace again. Look for slanted stripes: a structure carried upward appears as a stripe whose slope is its velocity.
Tracking clip: the ruler, with its tick marks, sets the scale; the white box is the part of the image the tracker follows.
read_the_figure.proves: If the bands line up with changes in the traces (a smooth rise before the first band change, a jagged cloud after), the regime labelling follows the data. If the kymograph shows slanted stripes, the flame carries coherent structures upward at a measurable speed.
if_wrong: Bands that change without any change in the traces: the classifier is reacting to something else, such as a change in lighting.
A kymograph without slanted stripes: no travelling structure at that resolution, or a window too short to see one.
A time axis that does not match the window named in the caption: a labelling slip or a re-zeroed clock.
A colour bar in pixels beside a y axis in millimetres: the colour values cannot be read in physical units.
must_check: The pixel scale is given in the figure or its caption. Here the ruler clip shows where it comes from but no value is printed.
The regime definition (which statistic, which threshold, which window) is stated. It is not stated here, and the bands alternate between onset and periodic.
Every panel states the same time zero, and a window in the caption matches the axis.
The colour scale has a unit and a defined linear or log mapping.
Height and width are defined the same way in every figure in the group.
as_drawn: Values read off by eye, about 5 percent.

Time series: height about 5 mm at ignition, about 30 mm near 100 s, about 55 mm at 155 s, then mostly 60 to 150 mm with the long-run centre near 105 to 115 mm. Width peaks near 20 mm at about 100 s, then stays near 11 to 14 mm.
Regime bands: Ignition Transient from about -8 to 155 s, Steady Laminar from about 155 to 181 s, then repeated switching between Flickering Onset and Periodic Flickering up to about 530 s.

Kymograph: the colour spans about 0 to 240 px. The flame tip fluctuates between about 55 and 110 mm over the 60 s window. The brightest widths, about 200 to 240 px, are at heights of about 30 to 45 mm.
Tracking clip: a ruler with visible marks at 7, 8, 9 and 10 and a white rectangle at the top of a vertical tube.

terms.meaning: A stage of flame behaviour, named from its signal: here ignition transient, steady laminar, flickering onset and periodic flickering.

The way a steady state turns into a sustained oscillation when a parameter passes a critical value: a pair of complex eigenvalues crosses the imaginary axis. Pool-flame flicker is commonly described as such an onset.
The closed orbit that the oscillation settles onto after the bifurcation. Its amplitude is set by the nonlinearity.
An image built by stacking a one-dimensional slice of every frame side by side, so that one axis is space and the other is time.
The speed at which a structure is carried along. On a kymograph it is the slope of the stripe.
Millimetres per pixel, found from a ruler or other object of known size in the same plane as the flame.
A signal sampled at regular intervals. Flame height and width are two time series of the same experiment.
The period after ignition when the flame grows and the burner and fuel pool heat up; the signal is not statistically steady.

remember: A time series needs a scale (mm per pixel) before its axis means anything physical.
A colour band is a claim about the signal; check that the signal supports it.
Flicker is oscillation about a mean: its size is the jaggedness, its frequency comes from a spectrum.
On a kymograph a slanted stripe is a travelling structure, and its slope is the speed.
A Hopf bifurcation turns a steady flame into an oscillating one when a control parameter passes a critical value, with amplitude growing as a square root of the distance beyond it.

understand.title: Why the series is split into regimes
understand.text: Statistics only make sense on a steady stretch. During the ignition transient the mean height is still climbing, so a standard deviation over that stretch mixes growth and flicker. Naming regimes tells the reader where each statistic may be taken.

understand.title: Why the kymograph
understand.text: A time series keeps only the tip. The kymograph keeps the whole flame at every instant, so that the tip trace becomes its upper edge while the interior shows how the flame width is distributed along the height.

understand.title: Why a ruler appears in the tracking clip
understand.text: Pixel counts are meaningless for distance until a known length is measured in the same units. The ruler beside the tube provides that known length and the white box is the region used to measure the pixel scale or follow the burner.

understand.title: What is unusual in the bands
understand.text: The bands do not form a clean sequence after about 180 s: onset and periodic alternate repeatedly. This is a reminder that the labels come from a classifier on a noisy signal, and nothing guarantees a monotonic path.

steps.title: Linear onset of an oscillation
steps.note: The standard normal form of a Hopf bifurcation, with z a complex amplitude, mu the distance from the critical point and omega the angular frequency. Reference only; the figure does not fit this equation.

steps.title: Amplitude and frequency of the limit cycle
steps.note: Below the critical value (mu negative) the amplitude decays to zero: a steady flame. Above it the amplitude settles at the square root of mu. Near onset the oscillation is small and grows continuously, which is why the flickering onset is a window rather than an instant.

steps.title: Pixels to millimetres from a ruler
steps.note: Read the ruler's tick spacing in pixels and divide the known length by it. All distances in mm in the series come from this single factor.

steps.title: Build a kymograph
steps.note: For each frame k, the flame width as a function of height h is one column; placing the columns side by side builds the image. The colour is the width.

steps.title: A stripe's slope is a velocity
steps.note: A structure that keeps its shape while moving upward sits at h = h0 + U t, a straight line in the (t, h) plane. Measure rise over run in physical units.

steps.title: Mean and fluctuation by regime
steps.note: Statistics are computed only over the samples of one regime R, so growth during the transient does not inflate the fluctuation.

worked.title: Speed of a stripe on a kymograph, with illustrative numbers
worked.problem: A bright stripe on the kymograph moves from a height of 20 mm to 60 mm in 0.8 s. What is its advection speed? (The numbers are illustrative; read the real stripes on figure 08 at higher zoom.)

solution.text: Rise over run in physical units.

worked.answer: 50 mm/s, i.e. 0.05 m/s. For a slanted stripe the speed is always height gained divided by time elapsed; a steeper stripe is a slower structure.

analyze.q: The height trace in the time series climbs smoothly to about 55 mm at 155 s, then turns jagged. List what changes physically at that point, and which part of the signal tells you.
analyze.hint: Compare the smoothness before and after, and the band colours.

analyze.q: The kymograph's time axis starts at 0 s but is described as the flickering-onset window. How would you check which part of run MVI_8036 it shows?
analyze.hint: Compare the tip fluctuation range with the series in figure 07.

analyze.q: The regime bands switch between tan and blue many times after 180 s. Give two explanations other than the flame switching back and forth.
analyze.hint: A threshold crossed by noise; a window-based classifier.

evaluate.q: Can the regime bands be used as ground truth for a statistic computed on one regime? What would you do to test the classification?
evaluate.hint: Hand-labelled segments, or a second independent criterion.

evaluate.q: The tracking clip is a 160 by 290 pixel crop. What can and cannot be claimed from it?
evaluate.hint: It shows where the scale comes from; it cannot show accuracy.

create: Redraw the time series with the regime classifier's criterion drawn underneath as its own trace (the quantity and the threshold), so that the band edges can be audited.
Design a kymograph figure with a physical-unit colour bar, a velocity reference line of a stated slope, and the window clock stated in the caption.

checks.q: Why are regimes labelled before the flame's statistics are computed?
checks.hint: What happens to a standard deviation if the mean is climbing?
checks.answer: A statistic like the standard deviation assumes a steady mean. During the ignition transient the mean grows, so including it mixes growth with flicker; computing on one regime avoids that.

checks.q: A stripe on a kymograph rises 45 mm in 0.9 s. What is its speed?
The kymograph shows no slanted stripes. List two reasons.
checks.answer: There may be no coherent travelling structures in that window, or the window or image resolution may be too short or too coarse to show them; the stripes may also be too faint at the displayed size.

checks.q: The colour bar of the kymograph is in pixels while its height axis is in millimetres. Does it matter?
checks.hint: Can you read a physical width from it?
checks.answer: Yes. A reader cannot convert the colour to mm without the scale, so the figure mixes units. The scale should be applied or stated.

checks.q: How would you make the regime labelling auditable?
checks.answer: Plot the classifier's input statistic and its threshold as a panel under the bands, state the window length, and show hand-labelled examples for each regime.
